title: Find Design Inspiration
bottom_line: Run `/design-inspiration:find`, answer a few design questions, and get a private page of 6 to 8 designs per app page to rate.

sections.heading: One command starts it, with an optional screen or focus

blocks.caption: The command. The part in brackets is optional.

before.label: You type
before.text: `/design-inspiration:find dashboard and settings` inside your app's repo.

after.label: You get
after.text: A private claude.ai Artifact page with 6 to 8 design screenshots for each app page, where you rate each design Love, Maybe or No and add notes.

blocks.text: It finds visual design references for the app in your repo and helps you choose between them. The optional argument names the screens or the focus, for example "dashboard and settings" or "onboarding". It counts as your answer to the Scope question. Without it, the skill asks.

blocks.title: When to use it
blocks.text: Use it whenever you want design ideas, inspiration, references, a moodboard, "something like Dribbble", a redesign direction, or "make this look better", even if you do not say "inspiration".

sections.heading: Have the Playwright CLI and the Artifact tool ready

cards.title: playwright-cli
cards.text: The Playwright CLI opens the design pages and takes the screenshots.

cards.title: claude.ai Artifact tool
cards.text: Publishes the shortlist. Without it, the shortlist stays a local HTML file, the skill tells you where it is, and ratings do not work there.

cards.title: plan-tools
cards.text: The design-inspiration plugin depends on plan-tools, which is installed with it.

blocks.text: Screenshots and browser files go into a scratch folder, never into your repo.

sections.heading: It works out your app from the code, then asks about design

nodes.label: Reads your repo
nodes.note: README, routes and pages, styles and design tokens, platform.

nodes.label: Asks design questions
nodes.note: Skips any question the repo already answers.

nodes.label: Writes the brief
nodes.note: The brief goes on the shortlist page.

blocks.text: It never asks what the app is, because the repo already says it. It asks scope, emphasis and priorities, mood and style, constraints and references, and whether to compare pairs first or go straight to a shortlist.

blocks.title: The five question topics
rows: Which app pages to find inspiration for (multi-select, built from the pages it found)
What the design must get right, for example clarity of data, speed for frequent use, trust, delight, or conversion
For example calm and minimal, bold and colorful, dark and technical, warm and friendly
Multi-select: keep the brand colors or logo, a component library to stay within, accessibility needs, sites you already like
Compare pairs first, or go straight to a shortlist
Always asked, because the repo cannot answer it

blocks.title: How your answers land in the brief
items: A question the repo or the argument already answers is dropped and noted as "(from the repo)" in the brief.
If you skip a question, the default is used and marked "(assumed)" in the brief.
If you type your own answer under "Other", it goes into the brief in your own words.

sections.heading: It searches the sites that suit each kind of app page

blocks.title: Which sources each app page gets

nodes.label: Dribbble, SaaSUI, Kombai, Collect UI, Behance
Awwwards, One Page Love, Recent.design and more

blocks.caption: Landing pages search Awwwards, One Page Love, Recent.design, SaaS Landing Page, Siteinspire, Land-book, Lapa Ninja and Behance.

blocks.title: Sources by kind of app page
rows: Dribbble, SaaSUI, the Kombai gallery, Collect UI and Behance
Awwwards, One Page Love, Recent.design, SaaS Landing Page, Siteinspire, Land-book, Lapa Ninja and Behance

blocks.title: How the search works
items: It uses several search angles per source and takes at most one design per designer.
It screenshots just the design image of each candidate, with no site header or sidebar.
It aims for about 16 usable candidates per app page, counted after looking at each screenshot.
It runs one extra round with new angles when the pool is short.

cards.title: A browser window opens
cards.text: Behance, Land-book and Lapa Ninja refuse a headless browser, so a visible browser window opens on your screen while they are searched.

cards.title: Bot checks are skipped
cards.text: A page that still shows a bot check is skipped, never worked around, and the final reply names it.

sections.heading: Comparing pairs first teaches it your taste

steps.title: A pairs page is published
steps.text: If you chose to compare pairs, it publishes a page showing two designs per app page that differ on one trait, such as density or palette.

steps.title: Pick and write notes
steps.text: On the page you pick the better one (or Neither) and write what you like and dislike in each.

steps.title: Choose Continue in the terminal
steps.text: It builds a taste profile per app page from your answers and shows new pairs until it has learned enough.

steps.title: One targeted search
steps.text: Then it runs one targeted search per app page: aimed at your taste, or, after a Love, at designs close to the loved one, including up to 3 by its maker.

items.label: Most pairs per app page
items.note: fewer when it has learned enough

items.label: Most designs by loved maker
items.note: by the loved design's maker, in the search after a Love

blocks.title: Ways to stop early
items: "Build the shortlist now" stops the pairs early.
Pressing "Love it, find more like this" on a design ends the pairs for that app page.

blocks.title: When pairs are skipped
blocks.text: Pairs are skipped when you choose to go straight to a shortlist, or when the claude.ai Artifact tool is unavailable.

sections.heading: You get 6 to 8 distinct designs per app page to rate

items.label: Designs per app page
items.note: fewer only when fewer good ones turn up

blocks.title: How the designs are picked
items: It picks 6 to 8 distinct designs per app page, dropping near-copies and spreading across sites.
It never pads the row with off-topic or weak designs: if fewer than 6 good ones turn up, it publishes those and tells you why and what would widen the search.
After the pairs, the cards are picked by fit to your taste, and a loved design is the first card.

blocks.title: What each card holds
rows: The design's name as the site shows it
The person or studio credited on the page (for galleries of shipped products that name no designer, the product or company)
One or two sentences tying it to this app and your answers
The concrete part worth borrowing (layout, type pairing, color, a component, density)

blocks.title: The published page
items: It publishes the shortlist as an Artifact, at the same link as the pairs page when there was one, with your taste from the pairs in the brief.
When you asked for several app pages, each one gets its own section with its own cards and its own overall note box, all in the same Artifact.
Rate the cards on the page. Ratings and notes are saved on the page and kept across reloads. Only you and editors can change them.
Artifacts are private by default.

sections.heading: The final reply gives the link and names what was left out

blocks.text: The reply gives the link and one line: "Rate the cards (Love / Maybe / No, notes optional), then run `/design-inspiration:plan <url>`."

blocks.title: It then names, by source and app page
items: Every source skipped because it was blocked.
Every source not searched because a step was refused.
Every source still empty after the extra round.
Every app page whose targeted search returned nothing usable or was skipped.
For each app page with fewer than 6 cards: how many it has, why, and what would widen it, such as a broader scope or a neighbouring screen type.

blocks.title: Other next steps
blocks.text: `/design-inspiration:mockup` can build a responsive mockup of your pages in the chosen look, which you comment on and have revised. `/design-inspiration:plan` reads your choices and plans how to apply them.

sections.heading: An invoicing app gets two sections of 7 cards

blocks.title: Example run in a small invoicing web app

steps.title: Run it with two screens
steps.text: You type the command with "dashboard and invoice editor".

steps.title: It reads the repo
steps.text: It learns it is a FastAPI + htmx invoicing app with a Tailwind palette.

steps.title: It asks three things
steps.text: It asks about emphasis ("fast data entry"), mood ("calm, professional") and constraints ("keep the green brand color").

steps.title: It searches in-app sources
steps.text: It searches Dribbble, SaaSUI, the Kombai gallery and Collect UI, the sources that suit in-app screens, from several angles each ("invoicing dashboard", "invoice editor form", "billing table", and so on).

steps.title: Three rounds of pairs
steps.text: You chose to compare pairs, so for three rounds you pick between two dashboards and two editors and say what you like in each, until you press "Love it" on an airy editor and the next search looks for designs close to it.

steps.title: The shortlist
steps.text: It publishes one page with two sections, Dashboard and Invoice editor, each holding 7 cards.

steps.title: You rate and plan
steps.text: You love two dashboards, mark one editor as Maybe with the note "only the line-item table", and then run `/design-inspiration:plan <url>`.

next_action.text: In your app's repo, run `/design-inspiration:find` with the screens you want, such as `dashboard and settings`.
next_action.detail: Without an argument, the skill asks which app pages to cover.
